title: Lattice Yang-Mills theory: spacing-uniform obstructions, the mass gap for every compact simple gauge group, and Lean certificate
description: Three papers and a Lean 4/Mathlib certificate. (1) Spacing-Uniform Lattice Inequalities Cannot Produce the Yang-Mills Mass Gap: a lattice gap uniform in lattice units forces vanishing continuum two-point functions; the open residual (Hypothesis R). (2) Mass Gap of Lattice Yang-Mills Theory up to the Dobrushin Ceiling: the sharp Hessian bound 4d, the sharp quarter for von Mises-Fisher laws on the three-sphere, and a lattice mass gap for four-dimensional SU(2) up to beta_W = 2/9. (3) Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional Lattice Yang-Mills Theory for Every Compact Simple Gauge Group (first posted as Hexagon preprint 2610.00341, 'in a Forest Gauge'): the gauge is fixed on straight lines meeting every plaquette once, so each free link has twelve partners; a unique free-boundary state, reflection positivity, exponential clustering and a transfer-matrix gap for SU(2) up to beta_W = 0.345 and SU(3) up to beta_W = 0.76 (plaquette blocks, constants certified in ball arithmetic); for every compact simple group, with kappa_G = h/(2 l_rho) the least Ricci curvature, a gap m_G(beta) = arccosh(1 + (kappa_G/(N|beta|) - 29/2)/12) for N|beta| < 2 kappa_G/29, past the curvature limit of the ungauged measure; and a conditional continuum step: a Dobrushin-Shlosman condition on one cube of fixed physical size, uniform along the continuum tuning, gives a mass gap in physical units for every continuum limit. What that requires: the cube condition holds at strong coupling; it forces the gauge-fixed links of a cube with trivial exterior to stay at mean distance at least (1-alpha)D/3 from the identity, so it fails at every fixed cube size once beta is large; for SU(2) a four-colour configuration with tetrahedral quaternions sharpens this to mean squared chordal distance at least 2(1-alpha) and mean distance at least 1-alpha, and for every compact simple group with the Hilbert-Schmidt metric of an irreducible representation the same colouring, through an SU(2) root subgroup and Schur's lemma, leaves at least the fraction 1-alpha of the Haar disorder, so the mean distance is at least (1-alpha)D/2; and bounds on single lines uniform in the exterior cannot give it (an SU(2) line with ten-step gap at most e^20 24^10 b^15 e^(-b/1280)). For SU(2) the cube condition needs n^4 >= 2(1-alpha) b/(5 L(b)), L(b) = 1 + log 24 + (3/2) log 9b, by a lattice Stokes inequality on discs of at most (n/2)(n/2+1) plaquettes, and a stationary flux configuration shows that the n^2 loss is of the right order; the continuum step holds for observables smoothed by the spatial gradient flow, whose transfer matrix is unitarily equivalent to the original one. At every n the mean distance of the gauge-fixed links from the identity is at least (1/9) max(6b,1)^(-1/2). For a Gaussian field the averaged cube coefficient is computed exactly: it equals 1 at every size and stiffness when the field is massless, and with mass m it is at most 1-(5/6)^4 (m l)^2/((m l)^2+160) on cubes of physical side between l/2 and l. In the quadratic approximation of the forest gauge itself (the Gaussian field of the Wilson action with the forest links fixed) the class sums of the cube coefficients are at least the cube size at every n and every stiffness, so the cube condition fails there; and no Bakry-Emery curvature argument for gauge-fixed SU(2) passes beta_W = 1/3. The cube estimate and the existence of the continuum limit are not proved, so the continuum Yang-Mills existence and mass-gap problem remains open. Lean: 70 theorems and lemmas, no sorry, standard axioms only.
